name: maybe_Object_DtorMultipleBases
summary: Destructor of a class with two base sub-objects: installs the class vtable, calls virtual slot 0x30 on each of the five owned child pointers, installs the sub-object vtable at +0xF4, then chains Container_ObjectDtor twice (once per base).
evidence: Still no callers and no constructor reference, so the class stays unknown; the only new context is the now-named base destructor Container_ObjectDtor, which confirms the destructor shape but not the class.

name: maybe_Svc_Cecd_ResetMailbox
summary: When the service flag at 0x007AF0E0 is set, writes the 24-bit state code into the state block at 0x007EF020, stores -1 in the status word at block-4, releases the owned sub-object and clears the flag bytes.
evidence: Still no callers and the only callee is the unnamed maybe_Object_ReleaseOwnedMember; the CECD attribution rests on the two global addresses alone, so the mailbox reading cannot be confirmed.

name: maybe_Svc_Cfg_ResolveTextLanguage
signature: u32 maybe_Svc_Cfg_ResolveTextLanguage(u8* configBytePtr, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 high)
summary: Reads the one-byte config block 0x000A0002 and returns the text-language index to use: the configured value when the system language supports it, otherwise that language's fallback (0 for JP, 1 for EN/FR, 6 for IT, 7 for ES, 0xB for ZH).
evidence: The full body shows the value read from config block 0x000A0002 is a small language/region index (0..11), not a character: the switch on the named Svc_Cfg_GetSystemLanguageCode returns 0/1/6/7/0xB, so the previous Font_MapChar reading was wrong. The per-language bitmasks are still not fully explained, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Regex_ParseBraceQuantifierB
signature: u32 maybe_Regex_ParseBraceQuantifierB(RegexParser* self, int* node, u32 arg3, int base)
summary: Consumes a brace at the parser cursor, parses the following token with Regex_ParsePredefinedClass and stores node kind 8 plus the parsed count; returns 9 when the input is not a brace form.
evidence: The only callee is the named Regex_ParsePredefinedClass and the 0x7B brace test is explicit, but nothing distinguishes this from the sibling 0x00510050 (node kind 7) or proves the repetition semantics.

name: maybe_Sound_Channel_GetBaseTime
summary: Picks one of four base constants (0xDF0C, 0xD930, 0xCD78, 0x30BB0) from the channel mode byte at +3, then adds 1500 or 10000 depending on the byte at +2; the unit of the constants is still unknown.
evidence: The only caller Sound_Frame_UpdateChannels fixes the sound subsystem, but the constants' unit and the unnamed 0x00518660 query leave BaseTime a guess.

name: maybe_Sound_SetPendingState
summary: Thin wrapper that forwards to 0x005177DC; the readable body is truncated because Ghidra marked that callee noreturn, so the conditional store described in the disassembly is not visible in C.
evidence: The decompiled body is a single call, so the +8 and +0x30 field semantics cannot be re-checked from C; the caller Sound_Decoder_DecodeFrame only fixes the subsystem.

name: maybe_Sound_CloseStream
summary: If the session-active flag at 0x007AEAA8 is set: sends service command 0x2C, closes the handle with svcCloseHandle, reports the failure when bit 31 of the result is set, and clears the flag.
evidence: Disassembly confirms the flag byte at 0x007AEAA8, svc #0x23 and the bit-31 error test; the only caller is the unnamed thunk 0x00501470, so the stream wording remains a guess.

name: maybe_Math_WrapFloatToU16
summary: Wraps a float into [0, limit) with std_Fmodf, truncates it to 16 bits through the VFP float-to-unsigned conversion and converts back to float; the u16 in the name is the intermediate truncation, the return value is a float.
evidence: Six named callers (Fx_Billboard_TransformPoint/Vector/Normal/CalcBasisMatrix, Math_Vector3_DistanceSquared, Fs_CheckPendingResult) confirm a shared math helper, but the callee 0x0051B7C4 still carries the poisoned Sound_Driver_Init name, so the family is unclear.

name: maybe_Err_NotifyServiceThread
summary: Loads the process handle at 0x007418D0, takes the current thread id and tail-jumps into the raw IPC sender 0x0051BDAC with (threadId, processHandle, arg1, arg2), i.e. command 0x1F with two handle parameters.
evidence: FACTS marks 0x0051BA34..0x0051CD40 as CTR SDK nn::err, so the previous Sound_ prefix is poisoned; the asm shows the TLS-based IPC block and svc #0x32 in the callee, but which err request 0x1F is remains unknown.

name: maybe_std_ThrowNarrowRangeEx
signature: void maybe_std_ThrowNarrowRangeEx(u32 str, u32 length, int pos, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Clamps length to pos+1 and tail-calls the range helper 0x001001C4; the three named callers (Actor_ApplyRecordTransform, Model_Instance_UpdateFromParams, Anim_IsInstanceBusy) all look like checked container access, so this is a shared bounds-check wrapper.
evidence: Three unrelated named callers confirm a shared helper, but the sole callee is itself named std_ThrowNarrowRangeEx, so the wrapper's own role (clamp versus throw) cannot be separated from it.

name: maybe_Fx_ClearParticleMarker
summary: Stores 0 into the particle's +0x6C word, runs the batch helper 0x0052E3C8 and advances the emitter frame; it deliberately leaves the three transform floats alone.
evidence: No callers; the only named context is Fx_AdvanceEmitterFrame, which fixes the Fx subsystem but not what the +0x6C word means.

name: maybe_Fx_SetParticleTransformAndClearMarker
summary: Copies three floats from the caller's array into the particle (+0x68, +0x64, +0x60), clears the +0x6C word, runs the batch helper and advances the emitter frame.
evidence: Same stores as 0x00527758 plus the explicit +0x6C clear; still no callers, so the transform interpretation rests on the three-float layout only.

name: Ui_ReleaseAnimObjectSlot
summary: Shutdown step of the UI system: releases the sub-object at +0x14, and when the loaded flag at +0x794 is set clears it and returns the handle at +0x768 to the global UI object pool through vtable slot 0xC.
evidence: The only caller is the now-named Ui_System_Shutdown, which fixes both the UI subsystem and the shutdown role; the handle is returned through the global pool object, so the slot reading holds even though the object type is not identified.

name: Sound_Registry_NotifyAll
signature: void Sound_Registry_NotifyAll(u32 registry, int begin, int end)
summary: Walks the circular notification list and calls vtable slot 2 on every node with the range [begin, begin+end), re-checking the static-init guard around each callback.
evidence: The only caller is the named Sound_Command_ExecuteList (opcode 0x31 broadcast), which supports both the sound subsystem and the notify-all-registered-listeners reading.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_ReleaseSlotEmitters
summary: When the slot still points at the live resource (slot+8 matches resource+0xC) and that resource is loaded or flagged, destroys the slot's emitter group with Fx_Group_DestroyEmitters and clears slot+4.
evidence: The guard tests that the resource is still alive (refcount non-zero or flags set), which contradicts the old IfUnused wording; the callers Gfx_Model_DrawOverlayPasses and Gfx_ModelInstance_SetMatrix fix the Gfx model-instance side.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_ReleaseBuffers
summary: Frees the two cached state buffers at +0x79C and +0x7A0 through the deleting-destructor thunks and clears both fields.
evidence: The callers are Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release and the overlay draw paths, so the object is shadow-pass or overlay state rather than a confirmed model instance; the release role itself is certain.

name: Mem_ReleaseRecordPairB
summary: Shared teardown helper: frees the owned pointers at record[0] and record[7] through the deleting-destructor thunk and clears both fields.
evidence: Eleven named callers across Gfx, Ui, Pack and Anim confirm a shared release helper; the B suffix stays because the layout differs from 0x00579794 (record[0] and record[3]).

name: Mem_ReleaseRecordTriple
summary: Frees the three owned pointers at record[0], record[3] and record[7], zeroing the six header words first; template sibling of 0x00579794 with one extra free.
evidence: The only caller is Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release and the body is a literal template copy of 0x00579794 plus the record[7] free, so the release role is certain even though the record type is not.

name: Mem_ReleaseRecordPair
summary: Frees the two owned pointers at record[0] and record[3], zeroes the six header words and returns the record pointer.
evidence: Same body as 0x00569CB8 minus the third free and the same caller Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release; the release role is certain, the record type is not.

name: maybe_Model_ReleasePartBuffers
summary: Frees the three per-part pointers at +0x298 (stride 4) and the two three-word blocks at +0xE88 and +0xEA4, clearing every freed field.
evidence: The only caller is Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release; the five frees are certain but whether the object is a model instance or shadow-pass state is still inferred from the offsets.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPartB

summary: Notifies the intrusive list and then walks the child list bounded by f_1E0 and f_1E4, calling virtual slot 0x1C on each child.

name: maybe_ItemBag_CountValidSlots

evidence: The only callee 0x0066AF08 is a mid-function label inside Party_FindEntryById, and the callers Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats and maybe_Ui_PanelGroup_Push do not settle what the 90-entry table is.

name: maybe_Ui_Slot_GetScale

name: Field_QueryFourPoints

name: maybe_Sound_SeqField_TestByte18
